findings.title: Clicking Back leaves the required keyboard transition untested
findings.evidence: target/verification-protocol.md:10 explicitly says "Click Back". surface-contract.json:15 requires back activation="Enter", traversal="Tab", and focus_after="introduction-heading"; surface-contract.json:18 requires "keyboard-back". checks/check_contract.py:35-36 explicitly requires sequential Tab or Shift+Tab traversal and Enter activation. The focus assertion at protocol line 10 checks only the outcome after a mouse click.
findings.condition: A Back control responds to mouse clicks and focuses the introduction heading but is unreachable through sequential keyboard traversal or does not respond to Enter.
findings.requirement: Exercise the back transition through sequential keyboard traversal and observed Enter activation, then verify the returned introduction and its heading focus.
findings.impact: Following every instruction in the protocol can leave the required keyboard-back acceptance obligation untested and miss a navigation failure affecting keyboard users.
findings.reasoning: Source mismatch in the written protocol; no website observation or claim about current website behavior. The existing close-help keyboard step does not activate Back.

findings.title: The procedure omits the required summary toggle and reopen sequence
findings.evidence: surface-contract.json:11-13 specifies opening help with Enter, closing it through summary with Space, then reopening with Enter; surface-contract.json:18 requires "help-toggle". target/verification-protocol.md:7 only says to open help using summary, without specifying Enter, and line 8 immediately closes help through the separate Close control. None of protocol lines 5-10 activates summary with Space or reopens help.
findings.condition: The separate Close control works, but summary Space activation fails to close help, Enter fails to reopen it, or summary keyboard activation is broken while pointer activation works.
findings.requirement: Exercise the declared open-help, toggle-help, and reopen-help transitions with their specified keyboard activations and verify their destination states.
findings.impact: The procedure can satisfy all its assertions while the required help-toggle check and declared summary keyboard transitions fail.
findings.reasoning: This is an omitted acceptance path in the document. It does not establish any website defect. The explicit Close/Enter step covers a different control and transition.
